subject: SLA remedy slabs and credit exposure for HelioTech
messages:
From: Simon Larsson <simon.larsson@heliotech.se>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: Clarification on SLA uptime bands and monthly credit exposure

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday — overall the demo looked great. Procurement and I are reviewing the standard SLA you shared. A couple of items jumped out that we need to resolve before we can move to legal:

- The uptime floor shown (99.9%) aligns to our expectations for online APIs, but HelioTech runs a mix of real-time and batch workloads. For batch-heavy endpoints we can tolerate lower availability; is there flexibility to define separate availability bands per route or workload class?
- The monthly service credit schedule in section 4 seems uncapped. For budgeting we need a hard cap (% of monthly invoice) on credits so our finance team can model exposure.
- We also need clearer carveouts for scheduled maintenance and a requirement for at least 30 days' notice for anything that could impact planned rollouts.

Can you propose an alternative that reduces HelioTech's exposure while keeping Redwood comfortable operationally? If you can show one counterproposal this week that maps to our needs we can move this to legal review.

Best,
Simon
Head of Platform Engineering
HelioTech AB

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:05:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Clarification on SLA uptime bands and monthly credit exposure

Hi Simon — appreciate the clear list. Answering inline at a high level and then a proposal below.

1) Separate availability bands: yes. We typically offer a single account-level availability commitment in the public template but we can define route-class exceptions ("batch endpoints") that carry a different uptime floor and altered remedy slabs. This is standard for customers that have mixed criticality.

2) Credit cap: we usually avoid hard caps for core APIs where availability is the primary product promise, but we can offer a capped remedy for non-critical/batch classes or propose a capped aggregate monthly exposure.

3) Maintenance notice: 30 days is reasonable for planned, customer-impacting maintenance; we can add notice + blackout windows for major releases.

Proposed counter (summary):
- Online-critical endpoints: 99.95% monthly uptime; remedy slabs: 99.95–100%: 0% credit; 99.50–99.95%: 10% credit; <99.50%: 25% credit.
- Batch/non-critical endpoints: 99.50% monthly uptime; remedy slabs: 99.50–99.90%: 5% credit; 98.00–99.49%: 15% credit; <98.00%: 30% credit.
- Aggregate monthly cap: credits payable for the account capped at 40% of the invoice for that month (applies across both classes).
- Scheduled maintenance: 30-day notice for major/region-affecting work; maintenance windows with standard carveouts (we exclude maintenance from uptime calc if notice provided and published).
- Latency: we can commit to P95 350ms for the critical online endpoints; batch endpoints would have a P95 target of 2s but not a financial remedy initially — we can discuss a performance SLA if latency is contractual.

If that sounds close, Grace and Neha are cc'd to confirm whether the 40% cap and the proposed slab numbers align with what we can offer for HelioTech at the current seat/commit level. I'm happy to include a redline of the template showing the alternate slabs.

Thanks,
Markus
VP, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Markus — thanks for the quick turn. A few follow-ups from procurement and finance:

- 40% cap: that's closer, but procurement wants an absolute floor on credits payable per incident period and an annual maximum exposure. They are asking whether we can get a 30% cap instead (they prefer lower) and a max annual exposure equal to 2x a single month's invoice.
- Latency remedies: P95 350ms for critical endpoints is reasonable — we would like that to be tied to a non-financial performance SLA initially (reporting + quarterly review), but we will push for a small credit (2.5% per month) if sustained P95 breaches happen for two consecutive months.
- For scheduled maintenance, procurement is insisting on a minimum 30 days' notice and a 72-hour "emergency maintenance" exception only with explicit opt-in.

Our legal team also asked whether Redwood can offer a single consolidated SLA exhibit that lists per-route classes, the specific remedy slab for each, and a one-line summary of the maintenance carveouts. If you can deliver that redline this week we can aim to start redlines in legal next week.

Simon

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 14:40:00 +0200
Subject: HelioTech counterproposal — approval to proceed with redline

Grace / Neha — looping you in. HelioTech (deal HLT-2026-042) pushed back on the cap and wants a lower aggregate credit cap (30%) and an annual maximum exposure (2x monthly invoice). They also want P95 latency to be tied to a small financial credit if the P95 target is missed for two consecutive months.

What I'm proposing we offer as a negotiable, sales-approved redline:

- Per-route classes in exhibit A: "online-critical" and "batch-noncritical" with distinct uptime floors.
- Online-critical: 99.95% monthly uptime; remedy slabs: 99.95–100%: 0%; 99.50–99.95%: 10%; <99.50%: 25%.
- Batch-noncritical: 99.50% monthly uptime; remedy slabs: 99.50–99.90%: 5%; 98.00–99.49%: 15%; <98.00%: 30%.
- Aggregate monthly cap: 40% by default, with a one-time sales concession to 30% for HelioTech if they sign a 12-month committed consumption addendum (we'd need finance sign-off).
- Annual cap: we decline the flat 2x-monthly permanent cap; instead offer an option: if customer signs the 12-month commitment, annual credit exposure capped at 2x single-month invoice.
- Latency: commit to P95 350ms for online-critical with quarterly reporting. Add a conditional credit of 2.5% for the account if P95 is missed for two consecutive months (applies only after a 60-day monitoring window).
- Scheduled maintenance: 30-day notice for planned events; emergency maintenance allowed only with explicit customer opt-in for any window that would materially affect availability.

Please confirm whether finance/legal need to weigh in on the concession to 30% and the 12-month commitment tie. If you approve, I'll produce a redlined SLA exhibit (single consolidated exhibit A with both classes) and send to Simon/procurement this week.

Thanks,
Markus
VP, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
